proposal.baseline: Static 100% allocation to the same US equity ETF (SPY) held without volatility scaling or rebalancing.
proposal.experiment: Simulate daily volatility-scaled positions on SPY from 2000-01-01 onward using the verified US equity proxy dataset (spec 8a512560a312ecdf8eff465bcdc88356bcc588772bef95227d37e6e13d0869ce). Scale exposure each day as target_vol / realized_vol (capped at 200% gross exposure). Incorporate double-transaction costs on rebalancing, borrowing costs on any leveraged notional, and slippage. Run the experiment on out-of-sample periods not used in any prior volatility-scaling tests. Record daily portfolio returns, drawdowns, Sharpe ratio, and turnover.
proposal.hypothesis: A volatility-scaled allocation to a broad US equity ETF (e.g., daily target volatility scaling of SPY to a fixed 10% annualized volatility level using 20-day historical volatility) will not produce statistically distinguishable risk-adjusted returns from a static unscaled buy-and-hold allocation after accounting for transaction costs, borrowing costs on leverage, and realistic slippage.
rejection_criteria: The volatility-scaled strategy fails any of the fixed preregistered gates (drawdown, sufficient_blocks, verified_accounting_causality).
The 95% confidence interval on the Sharpe ratio difference (scaled minus baseline) includes zero or is negative.
The strategy produces a maximum drawdown greater than the baseline by more than 5 percentage points.
After-cost and slippage-adjusted returns do not exceed the baseline on a total-return basis.

scope: Research proposal transfer; benchmark must measure any performance improvement
